slot.brief: Order given carbanions by stability including aromatic cyclopentadienyl anion; test whether student recognises aromaticity-driven stability.

stem: Which is the decreasing order of stability of the following carbanions?
options: Ethyl anion > allyl anion > cyclopentadienyl anion
Allyl anion > cyclopentadienyl anion > ethyl anion
Cyclopentadienyl anion > allyl anion > ethyl anion
Cyclopentadienyl anion > ethyl anion > allyl anion

verdicts.working: The cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic with 6 π electrons; the allyl anion is resonance-stabilized; the ethyl anion has no resonance stabilization. Thus stability decreases as cyclopentadienyl > allyl > ethyl.

working:
Cyclopentadienyl anion: $6\pi$ electrons, aromatic. Allyl anion: resonance stabilised. Ethyl anion: no resonance stabilisation. Stability: cyclopentadienyl $>$ allyl $>$ ethyl.

Independent check: The cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic with 6 π electrons; the allyl anion is resonance-stabilized; the ethyl anion has no resonance stabilization. Thus stability decreases as cyclopentadienyl > allyl > ethyl.
